title: Belling the Cat

parts.text: Hello, little friends! If a big cat tried to catch you every single day, what would you do? Is there a way to know the cat is coming, so you can run away in time?
Today, Huy Tells Tales will tell you a fable called Belling the Cat.

Long ago, in a small village by the river dike, behind a green bamboo hedge, there was a little house with a thatched roof and mud walls. Under the dish cupboard, behind some big rice jars, a whole family of mice lived.
Mama, what are we going to eat today?
In a little while, we will go out to the yard and pick up some fallen grains of rice.
But there was also Tabby Cat in that house. She had striped fur, bright eyes, and a long tail that swished from side to side.
Meow, meow! Tonight I will take another stroll around the kitchen and see what I find.

The cat walked very softly, because her claws were tucked away inside her soft paws. She liked to hunt in the evening, and her eyes could see well even in the dark. Often, before the mice heard a thing, the cat was already right behind them.
One night, Fat Mouse sneaked out to the pot of cold rice. Suddenly, a striped shadow leaped toward him.
Oh no, the cat! Run!
Fat Mouse rolled into a crack in the wall and escaped just in time.
The next day, Little Mouse went out to play near the baskets, and Tabby Cat almost pounced on him. Luckily, Mother Mouse pulled her child into the burrow in time.
Mama, I am so scared!
It is all right now, my good child. Mama is here.
Every night was the same. The whole mouse family lived in fear and worry. Grandfather Mouse, with his white whiskers, looked at his children and grandchildren and felt sad.
If this goes on, not one of us will dare to leave our burrow.
Yesterday I was nearly caught too, by the rice pounder.
Tomorrow night, the whole family will meet under the dish cupboard. We must find a way to deal with the cat!
The news spread to every nook and corner, from the burrow under the water jar to the cracks in the wall behind the kitchen.
The next night, the mouse family gathered. Grandfather Mouse sat in the best spot, on a torn piece of reed mat. The children and grandchildren sat around him in order.
Good evening, Grandfather.
Good evening, child. Please sit down.
Tabby Cat keeps hunting us. If anyone has a good idea, speak up so the whole family can hear.
All the mice began to whisper and chatter.
What if we dig a very deep burrow and hide underground, so the cat can never find us?
But then what will we eat, Fat Mouse? All the rice is up here.
Oh, you are right. Then we would be very hungry.
What if we all rush out and fight the cat!
But after saying it, Gray Mouse's legs shook and shook. The whole family looked at each other and shook their heads.
The cat is dozens of times bigger than we are. How could we ever beat her, child?
Just then, Tiny Mouse, the smallest of all, suddenly raised his hand, his eyes shining.
I have an idea!
Tell us, child. The whole family is listening.
The other day, I saw the farmer's buffalo wearing a bronze bell. Wherever the buffalo went, the bell went jingle-jingle.
All the mice perked up their ears to listen.
So let us tie a bell around the cat's neck! Wherever the cat goes, the bell will ring. When we hear the jingle-jingle, we can run away in time!
The whole space under the cupboard filled with clapping. The little mice jumped up and down with joy.
Wonderful! Wonderful!
From now on, we can eat our fill and sleep soundly!
So our children and grandchildren will be able to live in peace.
A young one from the Mouse family really is something special. So clever!
I saw a little bell lying outside the buffalo shed!
So a few mice ran out and worked hard to drag the bell back. The bell went jingle-jingle all along the way.
The bell was placed right in the middle of the space under the cupboard. Grandfather Mouse raised his hand, and the whole family waited quietly.
The plan is wonderful, and we have the bell. But now, who will go and tie the bell around the cat's neck?
Suddenly the whole space under the cupboard went completely silent. Only the crickets could be heard out in the yard. The mice looked at one another, and nobody said a word.
Mama, why is everyone so quiet?
Fat Mouse, you are the biggest and strongest in the family. Will you go?
Oh, Grandfather, I am too fat and I run too slowly. The cat would catch me first!
Ouch, all of a sudden my tummy hurts so much. Please let me go home first!
Then Fat Mouse held his tummy and scurried quickly into the crack in the wall.
What about Mother Mouse and little Út?
I must look after my little one. I cannot possibly go.
Mother Mouse led Little Mouse back into the shadows behind the water jar.
Gray Mouse, you just said we should rush out and fight the cat, didn't you?
Yes, but I have to guard the entrance of the burrow. If nobody guards it, it will be very dangerous!
Gray Mouse ran off as he spoke. One by one, the other mice found excuses and slipped away too.
And you, Tiny Mouse, who thought of the best idea?
Oh, I am only good at thinking. I am so tiny, I could never reach the cat's neck.
Then Tiny Mouse also bowed his head and tiptoed into the crack in the wall.
Now only Grandfather Mouse was left, sitting alone beside the bronze bell.
The bell is here, the good plan is here, and yet nobody dares to do it.
On the pile of straw in the corner of the kitchen, Tabby Cat stretched and pricked up her ears to listen.
Meow, what is that sound under the cupboard?
The cat is coming! The cat is coming!
Grandfather Mouse dashed into his burrow. The bell was left lying on the dirt floor.
Tabby Cat walked over and poked the bell with her paw. The bell went jingle-jingle and rolled into a corner of the kitchen.
What are those mice up to now? Oh well, I will go back to sleep.
The next morning, the sun rose behind the bamboo hedge. Grandfather Mouse called his children and grandchildren to gather around him.
Grandfather, so Tiny Mouse's plan cannot be used after all?
My dear children, saying is easy, but doing is hard.
No matter how good a plan is, if nobody can do it, it is worth nothing.
I understand now. Next time I will think of plans that we can really do.
I am sorry too, Grandfather, for using a tummy ache as an excuse yesterday.

From then on, the story of the mouse family was passed down by grandparents to their grandchildren. Even today, when someone comes up with a plan that sounds good but that nobody can carry out, people say it is like belling the cat.
Just like The Blind Men and the Elephant or The Plow Carved by the Roadside, the lesson of this story has become a well-known saying.
Little friends, having a good idea is wonderful. But what matters even more is daring to do it, and only promising what we can really do.
If you liked today's story, please ask your parents to subscribe to the channel Huy Kể Chuyện, so you can hear many more good stories. See you next time!

cast.role: Chuột mẹ hiền lành, thương con, viện cớ trông con nhỏ

facts.claim: Cả đàn chuột trong một xóm quê luôn bị mèo rình bắt, Chuột Cụ họp cả nhà bàn kế chống mèo
Một chú chuột nhắt nghĩ ra kế buộc nhạc vào cổ mèo để nghe tiếng nhạc mà chạy trốn, cả đàn vỗ tay khen hay
Khi Chuột Cụ hỏi ai dám đi đeo nhạc, ai cũng im lặng rồi lần lượt tìm cớ lủi mất
Bài học: nói thì dễ, làm mới khó, kế hay mà không làm được thì cũng bằng không
Mèo sống gần người, được nuôi để săn vật gây hại, ví dụ như chuột
Mèo có vuốt thu lại được trong đệm ngón nên đi nhẹ nhàng rình mồi, chân sau đặt lên dấu chân trước để giảm tiếng động
Mèo hiếu động lúc mặt trời lặn, nhìn tốt trong bóng tối hơn người, và ngủ nhiều
Mèo vểnh tai về phía có tiếng động để nghe ngóng
Truyện ngụ ngôn dùng hình tượng loài vật để nói về thói xấu của con người, gồm phần kể chuyện và bài học đạo đức
Bài học ngụ ngôn thường đúc kết thành thành ngữ, như Thầy bói xem voi, Đẽo cày giữa đường là ngụ ngôn dân gian Việt Nam
Aesop được xem là tác giả nhiều truyện ngụ ngôn nổi tiếng có loài vật biết nói và mang tính cách con người

look: Bối cảnh: một nếp nhà tranh vách đất ở xóm quê ven đê vùng đồng bằng sông Hồng, có lũy tre xanh bao quanh, sân đất, chuồng trâu nhỏ cạnh nhà. Trong bếp có chạn bát bằng gỗ mộc, chum vại và lu gốm nâu, nồi đất trên kiềng, rổ rá, thúng mủng, cối giã gạo bằng gỗ, đống rơm góc bếp, đèn dầu leo lét trên vách. Dưới gầm chạn là nơi họp của họ nhà chuột, trải một mẩu chiếu cói rách. Chiếc nhạc là quả nhạc đồng tròn nhỏ có quai, loại đeo cổ trâu, màu vàng đồng xỉn. Nhân vật là thú nhân hóa đơn giản, dễ thương, không mặc đồ hiện đại. Chuột Cụ: chuột lông xám bạc, râu dài trắng, lưng hơi còng, chống một que tre nhỏ, đội khăn xếp nhỏ màu đen và khoác áo dài ngũ thân màu the thâm. Chuột Nhắt: chuột nhỏ lông nâu nhạt, mắt to tròn, mặc áo cánh nâu ngắn. Chuột Béo: chuột tròn trịa lông nâu sẫm, áo cánh nâu căng bụng, khăn chít đầu. Chuột Xám: chuột lông xám, dáng gầy cao, áo cánh nâu, quần xắn gối. Chuột Mẹ: chuột lông nâu mềm, mặc áo tứ thân nâu ngoài yếm, váy đen dài, khăn mỏ quạ nhỏ, kín đáo. Chuột Út: chuột con nhỏ xíu, tóc để chỏm, mặc yếm có áo cánh ngắn ngoài. Mèo Mướp: mèo nhà lông mướp vằn xám nâu, mắt vàng sáng, không mặc quần áo, dáng tinh nghịch chứ không quá dữ tợn; khi rình thì mắt sáng trong bóng tối. Cảnh đêm dùng ánh đèn dầu vàng ấm và ánh trăng qua khe vách; cảnh sáng có nắng lên sau lũy tre. Không vẽ cảnh mèo bắt được chuột, chỉ vẽ chuột chạy thoát.
